renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: marker_box
  title: Marker intensity per cell
  description: |-
    Each box is the spread of the cells' mean intensity in one marker channel, one box per marker and segmentation method. It answers which markers carry signal and how bright they are against the rest of the panel.
    How to read: a marker whose box sits near zero has little signal or a failed stain, and a very wide box points to a marker expressed in only a subset of cells. Compare the segmentation methods within a marker: a shift between them means the masks capture different amounts of cytoplasm or neighbours. Open the table tile to inspect single cells.
    Note: intensities are shown on the asinh(x / 150) scale, a fixed cofactor of this catalog module and not read from the run. It keeps markers of very different brightness on one axis.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/labsyspharm/quantification/master/README.md
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: marker
    y: asinh_intensity
    color: segmenter
    labels:
      marker: Marker
      asinh_intensity: Intensity, asinh(x / 150)
      segmenter: Segmentation method

- component: figure
  id: marker_violin
  title: Marker intensity shape
  description: |-
    Each violin is the full distribution of the cells' mean intensity in one marker channel, one per marker and segmentation method. It answers whether a marker is unimodal or splits cells into positive and negative populations.
    How to read: two bulges mean a marker separates two populations, which is what a good lineage marker looks like. A single bulge close to the floor means a marker that stained little. Use it next to the box view, which hides modality.
    Note: intensities are shown on the asinh(x / 150) scale, a fixed cofactor of this catalog module and not read from the run.
  visu_type: violin
  dict_kwargs:
    x: marker
    y: asinh_intensity
    color: segmenter
    labels:
      marker: Marker
      asinh_intensity: Intensity, asinh(x / 150)
      segmenter: Segmentation method

- component: card
  id: measurement_count
  title: Intensity measurements
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of cell by marker measurements, and the ring splits them between nuclear stains and markers. It answers how large the quantification is and how the panel is composed.
    How to read: the figure below the ring counts distinct cells, so the ratio between the two is the panel size. A ring with a single role means the marker sheet does not flag the nuclear stain.
  column: cell_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: marker_role
  caption: measurements, by marker role

- component: card
  title: Typical marker intensity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median asinh intensity over every cell and marker in view, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how bright the panel is overall.
    How to read: filter to one marker with the selector to read its own level. A median near zero means the channel is mostly empty.
  column: asinh_intensity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Marker
  description: Pick one or more markers of the panel to restrict the tiles of this tab to them.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: marker

- component: interactive
  title: Marker role
  description: Keep nuclear stains, markers or both, which is how to read the panel without its counterstain.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: marker_role

- component: table
  title: Cell by marker measurements
  description: |-
    One row per cell and marker with the raw mean intensity and its asinh transform. Selecting rows filters the tab to those cells.
    How to read: sort by intensity to find the brightest cells of a marker, then open them in the spatial tile.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: cell_key

- component: advanced_viz
  id: spatial_cells
  title: Cells in the image
  description: |-
    Each point is a segmented cell placed at its centroid in the registered image, coloured by segmentation method or by the intensity of a marker chosen in the controls. It answers where cells and marker signal sit in the tissue.
    How to read: marker positive cells should form the structures the marker is known for, and a patchy or empty region may be a stitching gap or an out-of-focus tile. Compare two segmentation methods on the same image to see where one finds cells the other misses.
    Note: the origin is the top left of the image and y grows downwards, as in image coordinates.
  kind: spatial_cells
  roles:
    cell_id: cell_key
    x: X_centroid
    y: Y_centroid
    category: segmenter
    sample: sample
    area: Area

- component: advanced_viz
  id: shape_scatter
  title: Cell size against shape
  description: |-
    Each point is a segmented cell: its area in pixels on the horizontal axis and its eccentricity on the vertical axis, coloured by segmentation method. It answers whether the masks hold cells of plausible size and shape.
    How to read: most cells form a compact cloud. Points far to the right are large objects, often merged cells, and points at the top of the axis are elongated slivers, often fragments or debris. Compare the methods: one cloud shifted from the other means different masking rules.
    Note: eccentricity is that of the ellipse with the same second moments as the mask, from 0 for a circle towards 1 for a line. Neither quantity has a published cut-off, so no reference line is drawn.
    Source: https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/api/skimage.measure.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Cell area (pixels)
    y_title: Eccentricity
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: Area
    y: Eccentricity
    label: cell_key
    color: segmenter

- component: card
  id: cell_count
  title: Segmented cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of segmented cells in view, the bar splits them by segmentation method, and the line below gives the median and largest cell area. It answers how many cells were found and which method found them.
    How to read: a method finding many times more cells than another is usually splitting cells or segmenting nuclei rather than whole cells. Filter to one image to compare them fairly.
  column: Area
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: segmenter
  caption: cells, by segmentation method
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: median_area
  title: Typical cell area
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median cell area in pixels, and the bars rank the segmentation methods by their own median. It answers how large the segmented objects are.
    How to read: nuclear masks are smaller than whole-cell masks by design. A median far below the expected cell size points to over-segmentation, and one far above to merged cells.
  column: Area
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: segmenter
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median area, by segmentation method
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Cell roundness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median eccentricity of the segmented cells, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how elongated the masks are.
    How to read: tissue cells are rarely perfect circles, so a moderate median is normal. A box pushed towards 1 means many sliver-like masks, which points to over-segmentation along cell borders.
  column: Eccentricity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median eccentricity, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: area_box
  title: Cell area by method
  description: |-
    Each box is the spread of cell areas for one segmentation method. It answers whether the methods agree on how big a cell is.
    How to read: overlapping boxes mean the methods mask similar objects. A method with a much smaller box is segmenting nuclei or fragments, and a long upper whisker marks merged cells.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: segmenter
    y: Area
    color: segmenter
    labels:
      segmenter: Segmentation method
      Area: Cell area (pixels)

- component: interactive
  title: Segmentation method
  description: Keep the cells of one or more segmentation methods, to read each mask set on its own.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: segmenter

- component: interactive
  title: Cell area
  description: Restrict the tiles to cells within an area range, for example to drop debris or merged cells.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: Area

- component: table
  title: Segmented cells
  description: |-
    One row per segmented cell with its marker intensities, centroid and shape measures. Selecting rows filters the tab to those cells.
    How to read: sort by area or eccentricity to inspect the outliers of the size and shape plot.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: cell_key

- component: advanced_viz
  id: correlation_heatmap
  title: Marker correlation
  description: |-
    Each cell of the heatmap is the Pearson correlation between two markers across all segmented cells, with the rows annotated by segmentation method and marker role. It answers which markers are expressed by the same cells.
    How to read: strong positive blocks group markers of one cell lineage or compartment, and negative values separate exclusive populations. A marker with no correlation to anything either has no signal or marks a rare population. A nuclear stain should correlate with the other nuclear signals, not with membrane markers.
    Note: correlations are computed on asinh intensities, so a few very bright cells do not dominate them. No cut-off separates strong from weak correlation, so none is drawn.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: marker_row
    row_annotation_cols:
    - segmenter
    - marker_role

- component: interactive
  title: Segmentation method
  description: Show the correlation matrices of one or more segmentation methods.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: segmenter

- component: table
  title: Marker correlations
  description: |-
    One row per segmentation method and marker, with its correlation to every marker of the panel.
    How to read: sort a marker's column to list the markers that move with it.

- component: card
  id: brightest_markers
  title: Typical marker brightness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over images of each marker's median cell intensity, and the bars rank the brightest markers. It answers which channels carry the most signal.
    How to read: a wide gap between the brightest and the dimmest marker is normal in a panel, because stains differ in dynamic range. A marker near the floor in every image deserves a check of its antibody or exposure.
  column: median_intensity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: marker
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median intensity, brightest markers

- component: card
  id: marker_spread
  title: Marker variability
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median coefficient of variation of a marker's intensity across the cells of an image, and the box shows its spread. It answers how unevenly markers are expressed across cells.
    How to read: a high value means the marker is expressed in a subset of cells, as a lineage marker should be. A low value means a uniform signal, which suits a nuclear stain but is suspicious for a lineage marker.
  column: cv
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median variation, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: marker_median_bar
  title: Median intensity per marker
  description: |-
    Each box spreads the median asinh intensity of one marker over the images in view, one value per image, grouped by segmentation method. It answers how bright each channel is and whether the methods measure it alike.
    How to read: similar boxes across methods mean the measurement does not depend on the mask. A marker that is bright under one method only is picking up neighbouring signal or a different cell compartment.
    Note: intensities are shown on the asinh(x / 150) scale, a fixed cofactor of this catalog module and not read from the run.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: marker
    y: median_asinh
    color: segmenter
    boxmode: group
    labels:
      marker: Marker
      median_asinh: Median intensity, asinh(x / 150)
      segmenter: Segmentation method

- component: interactive
  title: Marker
  description: Pick one or more markers to restrict the tiles to them.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: marker

- component: table
  title: Marker summary per image
  description: |-
    One row per image, segmentation method and marker with the cell count, intensity quartiles and variation. Selecting rows filters the tab to them.
    How to read: sort by variation to find markers that are uniform or patchy.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: summary_key

- component: figure
  id: cells_per_image
  title: Cells per image
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of cells one segmentation method found in one image. It answers how many cells each image holds and whether the methods agree on the count.
    How to read: a method with far more cells than another on every image is splitting cells or masking nuclei. An image with very few cells under every method may be out of focus or mostly empty tissue.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: n_cells
    color: segmenter
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Image
      n_cells: Cells
      segmenter: Segmentation method

- component: card
  id: cells_per_image_card
  title: Typical cells per image
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of cells per image, and the bars rank the segmentation methods by their own median. It answers how dense the images are.
    How to read: the minimum and maximum show how much the images differ. A method that always finds more cells than another is segmenting at a finer level.
  column: n_cells
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: segmenter
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median cells per image, by segmentation method

- component: card
  title: Cells segmented
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of cells found across the images in view, and the bar splits it by segmentation method. It answers how much data the run quantified.
    How to read: the split shows how much each method contributes. Filter to one image to compare methods on the same tissue.
  column: n_cells
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: segmenter
  caption: cells, by segmentation method
  headline: true

- component: figure
  id: area_per_image
  title: Median cell area per image
  description: |-
    Each bar is the median area of the cells one segmentation method found in one image. It answers how large the segmented objects are and whether the methods differ.
    How to read: nuclear masks are smaller than whole-cell masks by design. A large difference between images under one method points to a change in magnification, tissue type or focus.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: median_area
    color: segmenter
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Image
      median_area: Median cell area (pixels)
      segmenter: Segmentation method

- component: interactive
  title: Segmentation method
  description: Keep one or more segmentation methods to compare them alone.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: segmenter

- component: table
  title: Segmentation per image
  description: |-
    One row per image and segmentation method with the cell count and area, axis, eccentricity and solidity medians. Selecting rows filters the tab to them.
    How to read: sort by cell count to find images that were segmented poorly.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: summary_key

- component: figure
  id: agreement_bar
  title: Share of cells matched by the other method
  description: |-
    Each bar is the share of one method's cells that hold the centroid of a cell of the other method, for one image and direction. It answers how far two segmentation methods agree on where the cells are.
    How to read: values near 1 mean every cell of that method has a counterpart in the other. The two directions of a pair are asymmetric by design, so a nuclear method against a whole-cell one reads high one way and low the other. Low values in both directions mean the methods find different cells.
    Note: a cell counts as holding another when its area, taken as a disc, contains the other's centroid. This catalog module defines the rule, and no published threshold grades agreement, so none is drawn.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: matched_share
    color: pair
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Image
      matched_share: Share of cells holding a cell of the other method
      pair: Comparison

- component: card
  id: agreement_card
  title: Typical agreement
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of cells that hold a cell of the other method, and the bars rank the methods by their own median. It answers which method is best covered by the other.
    How to read: a method with a low share has cells the other does not see, so its mask is finer or covers different structures.
  column: matched_share
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: segmenter
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median matched share, by segmentation method

- component: card
  title: Largest count imbalance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest ratio between the cell count of a method and that of the other method, and the bars rank the methods. It answers how much more one method cuts the tissue than the other.
    How to read: a ratio of 1 means equal counts. Large ratios mean one method splits or merges cells compared with the other, and the smallest ratio shows the opposite direction.
  column: count_ratio
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: segmenter
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: largest ratio, by segmentation method

- component: interactive
  title: Comparison
  description: Keep one or more directions of comparison, for example cells of one method holding a cell
    of the other.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: pair

- component: table
  title: Segmenter agreement
  description: |-
    One row per image, method and other method with the cell counts, their ratio and the matched share. Selecting rows filters the tab to them.
    How to read: sort by matched share to find images where the methods disagree most.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: pair_key
